name: LimiX-2

availability.notes: Weights (LimiX-2.ckpt, 1.63 GB fp32, single file) and inference code released 16 Sep 2026 on GitHub (limix-ldm-ai/LimiX, package 'LimiX' v2.0.0, not on PyPI, installed from git; Python >= 3.12, torch==2.9.1 pinned, flash-attn recommended) and Hugging Face (stable-ai/LimiX-2); a ModelScope mirror (modelscope.cn/organization/stable-ai) is linked. The repository contains only inference/model code (pyproject description: 'LimiX tabular foundation model inference'); no training, fine-tuning or synthetic-data-generation code is public. No hosted API exists and the weights license forbids offering one. The docs site (limix.ai/doc) mirrors the README.

architecture.type: Contextual Mechanism Network (CMN): cell-level dual-axis (sample-axis + feature-axis) in-context-learning transformer with decoupled feature and task pathways
architecture.parameters_note: Paper: 406.2M (largest of six scaling-study sizes, 12.5M-406.2M). Verified by summing tensor shapes in the released LimiX-2.ckpt: 406,232,101 parameters (transformer encoder 357.9M, regression decoder 24.7M, classification decoder 21.0M, rest encoders/adapters). README/TabArena round to 400M. Single checkpoint for all tasks. Paper notes LimiX-2 is ~4x smaller than TabFM.
architecture.layers: 24 dual-axis transformer blocks; each block: independent sample-axis attention for feature cells and for target slots -> independent SwiGLU FFNs (feature FFN and task FFN) -> asymmetric feature-axis attention -> residuals (checkpoint layer_arch 'smf')
architecture.attention_scheme: Sample-axis attention per column position: context rows attend to each other, query rows attend only to context (predictions invariant to query-batch composition; Q/K/V maps shared across feature columns but separate for the target stream; the K=4 target slots are concatenated for sample-axis attention). Feature-axis attention is asymmetric: feature cells attend to features + target, target slots attend only to features, with unshared Q/K/V for the two streams ('decoupled' feature-attention pipeline in code). All K/V heads are used in cross attention (v1 used a single K/V head). Q and K are RMS-normalised and queries are rescaled per head by a learnable length-dependent factor s_h=(1+w_h*log n)*beta_h (tanh-truncated; 'softmax scaling MLP'). Pre-normalised RMSNorm everywhere (Triton kernels), FlashAttention used at inference. 8 heads / hidden FFN dim 1024 come from the checkpoint config (nhead=8, hid_dim=1024), not the paper.
architecture.checkpoints: single multitask checkpoint (classification, regression, missing-value imputation, feature-attention-based causal skeleton recovery)
architecture.regression_head: distributional: target range split into B=5000 ordered bins (fixed borders on [-10,10] after target normalisation); softmax over bins, prediction = probability-weighted bin centres; decoder MLP linear-1024-GELU-linear-5000; replaces v1's MSE head
architecture.feature_embedding: Each cell x_ij -> R^256 via a two-layer MLP with RMSNorm + GELU shared by all columns; missing (and pretraining-masked) cells use one shared learnable embedding; column identity added via low-rank discriminative feature encoding (s=d/4=64-dim column code projected to 256); features handled in groups of 2 (features_per_group=2) with a small feature-group encoder. Targets encoded into K=4 slot embeddings of 256 dims (regression: MLP encoder; classes: orthogonally initialised embedding table of 10 entries; query targets: learnable MASK), plus a task-type (cls/reg) embedding. Classification head: MLP to 10 logits (cross-entropy). Heads sit at different depths: masked-feature reconstruction (MSE) head after layer 5 of 24, classification/regression heads on the final layer's 4 concatenated task slots, each preceded by a bottleneck post-adapter (linear-64/128-GELU-linear-256).
key_innovations: Contextual Mechanism Network paradigm: models the joint p(x, y | D_context) via multiple conditional prediction tasks per table instead of the PFN target-only p(y | x, D_context)

Decoupled feature and task pathways with asymmetric feature-axis attention (features <-> target vs. target -> features only) and separate SwiGLU FFNs; extra capacity allocated mainly to the task pathway
K=4 task-embedding slots per row instead of one task embedding; task-type embedding
Length-stable multi-head attention: QK-norm plus learnable length-dependent per-head query scaling; all K/V heads in cross attention; pre-norm RMSNorm
5000-bin distributional regression head (was MSE) and depth-specific heads with bottleneck post-adapters (reconstruction head at shallow depth 5, task heads at depth 24)
Expanded SCM prior (causal motifs, graph transformations, new edge functions, multi-objective task selection) and three interleaved mask granularities (cell, column, block)
Feature-attention scores recover causal skeletons (mean F1 0.7972 on six causal-discovery datasets, best among TFMs and dedicated methods)
Log-linear Elo-vs-parameters scaling law over six sizes (12.5M-406.2M) with no saturation; guided the scale-up from LimiX-16M

capabilities.max_classes_note: Hard limit: the classification head is 10-wide (checkpoint max_num_classes=10) and LimiXPredictor raises ValueError for n_classes > 10 (or < 2). The paper excluded the 12 TALENT datasets with > 10 classes. TabArena's wrapper handles > 10 classes with an ECOC ManyClassClassifier (many_class_threshold=10).
capabilities.max_features_note: No documented or coded hard limit; feature count is padded to a multiple of 2 and memory-bound (adaptive SVD budget, some ensemble members reduce features via TruncatedSVD to 32/64/128 components, polynomial-interaction members are dropped on CUDA OOM). The earlier LimiX (v1) usage tips recommended < 10,000 features; nothing equivalent is published for LimiX-2. Paper: rank stays low across 10-100+ features and 'generally improves as dimensionality increases' on TALENT.
capabilities.max_samples_note: No hard cap: the entire training table is the in-context set in every forward pass (no subsampling/retrieval in v2), so cost grows with training rows. TabArena maintainers needed 8 h (instead of 1 h) budgets on the nine largest/widest datasets (APSFailure took ~3.25 h per split on an RTX PRO 6000 96 GB) and 2 h elsewhere. v1 usage tips recommended < 50,000 samples; LimiX-2 publishes no recommendation. Paper: strongest relative performance around 10^4 samples on BCCO, 'medium-to-large' datasets on TALENT.
capabilities.categorical_features: Handled per ensemble member by the preprocessing pipelines (ordinal / ordinal-shuffled / strict-ordinal-with-feature-shuffle / one-hot / numeric / none encodings; feature_encoder_mode 'train_unknown_nan'); optional categorical_features_indices argument; pandas category/string columns are cast to object and encoded; datetime-like string columns are auto-detected and expanded into numeric date features. Pretraining samples numbers of categorical vs continuous features explicitly.
capabilities.other: Missing-value imputation as a first-class task (task_type='Feature_imputation', reg_default_noretrieval_MVI_v2.json); naturally missing cells share the mask embedding. Causal skeleton recovery from feature-attention scores (Table 7: F1 0.7143 Sachs, 0.8617 UF, 0.7013 CausalChamber, 0.7829 PATHFINDER, 0.7846 DIABETES, 0.9385 PIGS; mean 0.7972 vs 0.6591 EXAONE Tabular). Conditional likelihoods can score anomalous entries (mentioned, not evaluated). Regression outputs are returned on the original target scale. Predictions are invariant to query-batch composition by design (GPU numerics drift ~2.6e-3 observed in TabArena tests). The v1 'data generation' capability is not advertised for LimiX-2.

pretraining.synthetic_prior_summary: Five-stage SCM engine inherited from LimiX v1 and expanded. (1) Hyperparameter sampling: per dataset sample size, numbers of continuous and categorical features, task type and the context/query split position are drawn, with each hyperparameter's sampling distribution itself chosen from a family (normal, uniform, beta). (2) DAG generation: the graph is built hierarchically by recursive expansion of local causal structures specified as causal motifs (chain, confounder, collider) at several granularities, then randomly perturbed by topology-constrained transformations (edge redirection, local path replacement, node-level transformations) that keep acyclicity. (3) SCM propagation: root nodes sampled from randomly chosen distributions; X_i = f_i({g_ij(X_j)}_{j in PA(i)}, eps_i) with edge functions g: MLPs, CNNs and decision trees (from v1) plus new linear mappings, kernel functions, piecewise functions, periodic functions and multiplicative interactions, all composable; parent aggregation f: simple averaging, weighted or neural aggregation; stochastic noise eps_i. (4) Feature/target sampling: only a subset of SCM variables is observed; variable sampling is a multi-attribute selection problem using coarse task descriptors (subgraph structure, feature redundancy) filtered by a multi-objective mechanism for structural and statistical diversity. (5) Task adaptation: stochastic observation transforms (linear scaling, monotonic nonlinear, log, exp, random compositions); classification targets via random discretisation of the continuous target into a varying number of intervals with varying class frequencies/imbalance; regression targets with random scale, skewness and tail adjustments. Episodes split rows into disjoint context and query sets; three masking schemes (individual cells, whole columns across query rows, blocks) are interleaved.
synthetic_prior_types: SCM on hierarchical DAGs built from causal motifs with graph transformations
pretraining.num_synthetic_datasets_note: Not stated. The paper only says 'a large number of datasets' and that the corpus 'can be expanded on demand'; no dataset, episode or token counts, and no row/feature/class sampling ranges are given.
pretraining.real_data: none (pretrained exclusively on synthetic SCM data; TabArena/TALENT/BCCO used only for evaluation)
pretraining.objective: Context-Conditional Masked Modeling (CCMM): for query rows, predict the target from the query's observed features plus the labelled context (cross-entropy for C-way classification; 5000-bin bucketised distributional loss for regression, replacing v1's MSE) and reconstruct masked query features q_theta(x_ij | x_i,-pi_i, X_ct, y_ct) through a shallow-depth reconstruction head; masks at cell, column and block granularity; targets p(x, y | D_context).
pretraining.training_cost_note: The technical report gives no optimizer, learning-rate schedule, step count, batch/context sizes, precision, GPU type/count, GPU-hours or cost; the repo has no training code. Only stated: the scaling study trained six sizes (12.5M to 406.2M parameters) under 'a fixed data-generation, optimization, and inference recipe'. LimiX v1's report was similarly silent on hardware (its scaling study spanned 1e11-1.7e12 training tokens).
pretraining.curriculum: not disclosed (no context-length or difficulty curriculum described; v1 mentioned mask ratios sampled in [0.1, 0.4] and solvability-aware task sampling, v2 does not repeat these numbers)

icl.context_note: No fixed context window: the whole training set is passed as context in every forward pass (checkpoint/inference impose no row cap); practical limit is GPU memory and time. Query rows are processed in batches (test_batch_size default 16384 per forward, 'full_first' mode tries the full query set then halves on CUDA OOM). Context rows attend to each other; queries attend only to context.
icl.large_dataset_strategy: None built in for v2: no subsampling, no kNN/attention retrieval (v1's two-pass attention-based retrieval was removed; the v2 predictor rejects use_retrieval=true), no bagging over context chunks. Memory management only: query batching with OOM back-off, adaptive per-forward SVD component budget from free CUDA memory, polynomial-interaction members disabled after OOM, optional pipeline-parallel ensemble members across several GPUs (gpu_ids). TabArena therefore ran large datasets with 8 h budgets.
icl.test_time_ensembling: Default packaged configs: 32 preprocessing-pipeline members for classification (cls_default_noretrieval_v2.json), 8 for regression and 8 for imputation. Members differ in feature-distribution rebalancing (quantile-normal/uniform on all data or subsets, KDI, robust scaling, Yeo-Johnson power, none), optional TruncatedSVD components (32/64/128) appended to the original features, categorical encoding (ordinal strict/shuffled, one-hot, numeric, none), feature permutation (rotate/shuffle), a fingerprint feature encoder and polynomial-interaction generators (10/50/100 features). Each member is one forward pass over the full context; classification logits are averaged before a softmax with temperature 0.9, bucket-regression members are averaged in log-prob space; mixed precision on GPU; seed 0. TabArena used exactly these packaged configs (32 and 8 members); n_estimators can truncate the list.
icl.fine_tuning: Not supported by the released code (inference only) and not discussed in the LimiX-2 report; the TabArena wrapper updates no parameters. (The LimiX v1 report described fine-tuning with retrieval-guided episodes, but no fine-tuning code ships in the current repository.)
icl.inference_notes: Entry point inference.predictor.LimiXPredictor (routes v1_0/v2_0 by checkpoint arch_version 2.0) or CLI 'LimiX-infer'; predict(x_train, y_train, x_test, task_type) returns class probabilities (n_query, n_classes), regression values on the original scale, or the imputed matrix. Options: mix_precision (autocast), outlier_remove_std=12, softmax_temperature=0.9, deterministic mode, test_batch_size, preprocess_num_jobs (CPU-parallel preprocessing, default 16), gpu_ids for pipeline parallelism, on-disk preprocessing cache. CUDA strongly recommended; CPU works but is far slower and disables mixed precision.

speed.hardware_note: The paper reports no timing or hardware. TabArena's official run (2026-09-17): one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB) per fit on 64 SkyPilot workers, torch 2.13, LimiX commit 774aa3e1, checkpoint revision 20c07a07.
speed.memory_note: Checkpoint 1.63 GB (fp32). TabArena's wrapper budgets a 10 GB baseline (network + activations + per-member preprocessing copies) plus 5x the dataframe size. The predictor halves the query batch on CUDA OOM and sizes SVD components from free GPU memory; memory grows with context rows x features because the full training table is attended in every member forward pass.
speed.speed_claims: TabArena (full 51-dataset suite, 8x1 protocol): median fit 30.94 s per 1K rows and predict 9.03 s per 1K rows, the slowest of the top group (TabPFN-3.5: 5.7 s / 0.5 s; TabFM+: 20.0 s / 7.5 s; Mitra-v2: 57.1 s / 0.8 s); maintainers describe it as 'the accurate-and-slow end of the Pareto front'. Nine large/wide datasets needed an 8 h time limit and every other dataset 2 h instead of the 1 h default (recorded protocol deviation); APSFailure splits took ~3.25 h each. The paper makes no speed claims.
speed.inference_cost_note: No API or pricing; self-hosted GPU inference only, and the weights license prohibits hosted/API or any commercial deployment.

differences_vs_predecessor: Predecessor: LimiX v1 (LimiX-16M, 16.52M params, arXiv 2509.03505, released 29 Aug 2025; Apache 2.0). Changes in LimiX-2: (1) Scale: ~25x more parameters (16.5M -> 406.2M), embedding 192 -> 256, 12 blocks (v1: two feature-axis passes + one sample-axis pass per block, shared FFN, pre-LN LayerNorm) -> 24 dual-axis blocks with pre-norm RMSNorm; capacity added mainly to the task pathway. (2) Decoupled pathways: v1 routed features and target through the same attention/FFN; v2 uses separate sample-axis attention and separate SwiGLU FFNs for feature and task streams, asymmetric feature-axis attention with unshared Q/K/V, and K=4 task-embedding slots plus a task-type embedding instead of one task embedding. (3) Attention: all K/V heads in cross attention (v1: one K/V head), QK-norm and learnable length-dependent query scaling for length stability. (4) Heads: 5000-bin distributional regression instead of MSE; heads attached at different depths (masked-feature reconstruction at a shallow layer, classification/regression at the top) with bottleneck post-adapters. (5) Prior: same five-stage SCM pipeline but with hierarchical causal-motif DAGs and topology-constrained graph transformations, new edge functions (linear, kernel, piecewise, periodic, multiplicative; composable), several parent-aggregation strategies, multi-objective feature/target selection and richer observation transforms; three interleaved mask granularities retained. (6) Inference: v1's attention-guided two-pass retrieval ensemble (4 pipelines for classification, 8 for regression, retrieval of context samples/features from attention scores) is removed; v2 uses larger no-retrieval preprocessing ensembles (32 / 8 members) over the full context, and regression returns the original scale. (7) Scope: v2 advertises classification, regression, imputation and causal-skeleton recovery; v1 additionally advertised data generation and fine-tuning. (8) License: v1 weights Apache 2.0 -> v2 weights non-commercial; code Apache-derived with attribution clause. (9) Results: TabArena Elo 1345 -> 1935 (paper; 1344 -> 1943 in TabArena's own runs), TALENT 1227 -> 1506, BCCO 1230 -> 1432. Sibling LimiX-2M (Wang et al., arXiv 2606.04485, ICML 2026; 1.92M params, d=96, 6 heads, 12 blocks; released 10 Nov 2025) is a separate lightweight v1-family model whose contributions are the RaBEL radial-basis numeric embedding and the reordered sample-attention -> FFN -> feature-attention block; LimiX-2 adopts that block order but not RaBEL (it keeps a linear/MLP numeric encoder). '2M' denotes 2 million parameters, not version 2.

notes: Release date: weights/code published 16 Sep 2026 (README news); arXiv v1 submitted 15 Sep 2026; HF repo created 15 Sep 2026. Author list: 'LimiX Team' (Stable AI & Tsinghua University), project design/lead Xingxuan Zhang and Peng Cui, ~58 named contributors. Numbers the paper does NOT give (all set to null / 'not disclosed'): training optimizer, steps, batch/context sizes, hardware, compute or cost; number of synthetic datasets; explicit feature/sample limits; inference timings; attention-head count and FFN width. Heads (8), FFN hidden dim (1024), K=4 slots, 5000 buckets, 10-class head and the exact parameter count (406,232,101) were read from the config and tensor shapes embedded in the released LimiX-2.ckpt (sources[10]) and agree with the paper's 24 layers, d=256, K=4, B=5000 and 406.2M. Elo values differ between the paper (1935, computed against leaderboard scores accessed 2026-09-15) and TabArena's own maintainer run (1943, 96 entrants, longer time limits); the site's tabarena.json should be treated as authoritative for the leaderboard number. The paper's TabArena table lists 'TabPFN-3' (1632) whereas TabArena's run compares against TabPFN-3.5 (1861). LimiX-2M (2 million params) is a different, older model than LimiX-2. The GitHub code license's Section 10 says weights distributed under it are part of the Work, but the LimiX-2 weights are distributed under the separate non-commercial license, so commercial use of LimiX-2 requires a commercial agreement regardless of the code license.
